title: VS Code & Python Environment Setup
objectives: Install VS Code and Python on your machine
Configure the Python extension and Pylance
Create and activate a project virtual environment (.venv)
Run and debug your first Python program inside VS Code
Verify the development environment is ready for the remaining course
mechanism: Local Python interpreter and virtual environment isolation
purpose: Clean reproducible environment for local AI development
ahaMoment: Environment isolation prevents dependency hell when building complex AI pipelines.

title: Local LLM & AI Coding Assistant Setup
objectives: Install Ollama and download a local coding model
Verify the local model works through the Ollama CLI
Connect VS Code to the local model using GitHub Copilot or Cline
Generate code using the local AI assistant
Confirm the complete AI coding workflow works offline
mechanism: Local model inference via Ollama server API
purpose: Private, latency-free offline code generation
ahaMoment: Running local LLMs allows zero-cost rapid prototyping without privacy or API rate-limit concerns.

title: First AI Project, React Frontend & GitHub
objectives: Build a command-line chatbot powered by your local Ollama model
Scaffold a FastAPI backend with a health endpoint
Create a React application using Vite
Connect the React frontend with the FastAPI backend
Initialize Git, commit the project, and publish it to GitHub
mechanism: Client-server REST architecture connecting React UI to FastAPI to Ollama
purpose: Full-stack foundation for AI-powered web applications
commonFailureModes: Synchronous blocking calls in FastAPI endpoints
ahaMoment: Separating AI inference into FastAPI endpoints keeps frontends responsive and allows seamless backend swaps.

title: Reading & Processing Structured Data
objectives: Create synthetic healthcare plans and claims datasets
Load and clean structured CSV data using Pandas
Store the processed data in a SQLite database
Write SQL queries to answer common healthcare questions
Document reusable SQL queries for later chatbot integration
mechanism: Relational database storage and SQL query execution for structured healthcare data
purpose: Structured data querying and analytics engine for healthcare claims and plan rules
commonFailureModes: NULL handling errors in aggregate functions
ahaMoment: Combining SQL queries with LLMs allows exact deterministic lookup of numbers and claim rules rather than fuzzy LLM hallucination.

title: Reading & Processing Unstructured Data
objectives: Extract text from healthcare PDFs and Word documents
Perform OCR on scanned enrollment forms
Scrape useful content from a public healthcare webpage
Clean and normalize extracted text from multiple sources
Store the processed text files for knowledge-base creation
mechanism: Multimodal document parsing and text normalization pipeline
purpose: Converting messy healthcare PDFs, scanned forms, and web pages into clean cleanable text stream
ahaMoment: Document parsing quality directly bottlenecks RAG accuracy—garbage text in means garbage context out.

title: Building the Knowledge Base
objectives: Convert structured and unstructured healthcare data into a unified knowledge base
Split long documents into retrieval-friendly chunks
Attach metadata such as source, plan type, and document section to every chunk
Export all processed records into a knowledge_base.jsonl file
Validate chunk quality before using them for embeddings
mechanism: Semantic text splitting and rich metadata tagging into structured JSONL
purpose: Preparing high-quality retrieval units for vector search
commonFailureModes: Truncating sentence mid-context with naive character splitters
ahaMoment: Chunk overlap and metadata retention preserve critical context boundaries that single vectors would otherwise lose.

title: Embeddings Explained
objectives: Understand how text is converted into vector embeddings
Generate embeddings for every knowledge base chunk
Store embeddings alongside the original documents
Visualize embedding clusters using PCA
Analyze whether similar healthcare concepts cluster together
mechanism: High-dimensional dense vector space projection of semantic text
purpose: Mapping semantic meaning to geometric distance for context matching
commonFailureModes: Poor embedding model choice for healthcare terminology
ahaMoment: Semantic similarity is spatial distance—related concepts cluster close together regardless of exact keyword overlap.

title: Vector Databases Overview
objectives: Learn the role of vector databases in RAG applications
Set up a local Chroma vector database
Create a cloud-based Pinecone index for comparison
Compare local and managed vector database solutions
Select the most suitable database for the chatbot project
mechanism: Indexed vector storage and ANN (Approximate Nearest Neighbor) similarity search
purpose: Fast sub-millisecond retrieval over millions of high-dimensional vectors
commonFailureModes: Memory leak on local Chroma instances
ahaMoment: Vector databases enable instant semantic retrieval that standard SQL inverted indexes can never achieve.

title: Building & Populating the Vector Database
objectives: Load knowledge base embeddings into the vector database
Store documents together with metadata for filtering
Verify that every knowledge base chunk has been indexed
Test semantic search with healthcare-related questions
Evaluate retrieval quality and metadata filtering
mechanism: Batch insertion of vectors, documents, and payload metadata into indexed collections
purpose: Deploying a queryable vector index for healthcare domain knowledge
ahaMoment: Filtering vectors by metadata (e.g. plan_type='PPO') before similarity search drastically increases retrieval precision.

title: The Retrieval & Matching Engine
objectives: Build a query router that decides between SQL, vector search, or hybrid retrieval
Implement structured data lookup for plans and claims
Implement semantic retrieval from the vector database
Merge and deduplicate results from multiple retrieval sources
Evaluate retrieval accuracy using a diverse set of healthcare questions
mechanism: Hybrid retrieval routing and reciprocal rank fusion across SQL and Vector DBs
purpose: Universal matching engine handling both numerical relational queries and semantic medical text queries
commonFailureModes: Poor score normalization when merging SQL and vector results
ahaMoment: Combining SQL precision for hard numbers with Vector DB recall for fuzzy knowledge solves 99% of RAG failure modes.

title: RAG End-to-End & LLM API Basics
objectives: Connect the retrieval engine to an LLM to build a complete RAG pipeline
Configure a local or hosted LLM provider using the OpenAI-compatible SDK
Create a grounded prompt that answers only from retrieved context
Generate answers using retrieved knowledge
Evaluate chatbot responses against the retrieval-only baseline
mechanism: Retrieval-augmented generation context injection into LLM prompt template
purpose: Grounded factual generation without hallucination
ahaMoment: Forcing the LLM to act purely as an synthesizer of provided context turns a creative text generator into a reliable factual agent.

title: Prompt Engineering Fundamentals
objectives: Understand zero-shot, few-shot, and chain-of-thought prompting
Design multiple system prompt variations for the chatbot
Compare prompts based on accuracy, compliance, and tone
Evaluate prompt performance using a fixed question set
Finalize the production-ready system prompt
mechanism: In-context learning instruction design and reasoning structure steering
purpose: Optimizing model accuracy, compliance, and structured output adherence through natural language instructions
ahaMoment: Adding a simple 'Step-by-step reasoning before final answer' prompt instruction reduces logic errors by over 50%.

title: Advanced Prompting: Function Calling & Structured Outputs
objectives: Define tool schemas for healthcare-related chatbot functions
Implement LLM function calling with automatic tool execution
Validate structured outputs using Pydantic models
Log tool calls for debugging and auditing
Test different user queries to verify correct tool selection
mechanism: JSON schema representation of native functions exposed to LLM reasoning loop
purpose: Enabling LLMs to execute external Python functions and return typed structured JSON
commonFailureModes: Schema validation error from invalid LLM parameter types
ahaMoment: Constraining LLMs to emit strict JSON schemas transforms unpredictable text outputs into programmatic API integrations.

title: Fine-Tuning: Concepts & When to Use It
objectives: Understand when fine-tuning is more appropriate than prompting or RAG
Identify chatbot issues that fine-tuning can solve
Create a high-quality fine-tuning dataset
Validate and organize the dataset into training and test sets
Prepare the project for model fine-tuning
mechanism: Parameter weight updates on domain-specific input/output dataset pairs
purpose: Customizing model tone, style, specialized jargon, or latent task behavior
commonFailureModes: Fine-tuning to memorize facts instead of using RAG
Catastrophic forgetting of base model capabilities
Dirty training data causing toxic outputs
ahaMoment: Use RAG for dynamic knowledge retrieval and fine-tuning for static style/format adaptation—never confuse the two!

title: Fine-Tuning: Hands-On with LoRA & QLoRA
objectives: Train or fine-tune an LLM using LoRA or the OpenAI fine-tuning workflow
Load and evaluate the fine-tuned model
Compare the base model and fine-tuned model on unseen test cases
Measure improvements in tone, consistency, and response quality
Document whether fine-tuning provides measurable benefits for the chatbot
mechanism: Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning (PEFT) using low-rank matrices and 4-bit quantization (QLoRA)
purpose: Resource-efficient model specialization on consumer hardware
ahaMoment: QLoRA enables fine-tuning 7B+ parameter models on a single GPU with minimal memory overhead and zero degradation in reasoning.

title: Chatbot Backend & API Integration
objectives: Create a /chat API endpoint for the healthcare chatbot
Integrate retrieval, function calling, and LLM response generation
Implement session-based conversation management
Build a conversation history endpoint
Test the complete backend API using Postman or cURL
mechanism: Stateful REST API endpoint orchestrating RAG, session context, and LLM calls
purpose: Exposing unified conversational API backend for healthcare chat frontends
commonFailureModes: Memory bloat on long session histories
Race conditions on concurrent API calls
Thread locking in sync FastAPI handlers
ahaMoment: Decoupling session state from the AI inference engine allows stateless horizontally scalable API servers.

title: Chatbot Frontend Development
objectives: Build an interactive chat interface for the chatbot
Connect the frontend to the backend chat API
Maintain conversation history across user interactions
Add a healthcare plan selector and new conversation option
Validate end-to-end communication between frontend and backend
mechanism: Reactive UI components binding client input to backend API endpoints
purpose: Providing responsive visual interface for user interaction with healthcare AI
ahaMoment: Maintaining clean message state arrays in UI prevents duplicate message rendering and lost chat history.

title: Full-Stack Integration & Streaming Responses
objectives: Implement real-time streaming responses from the LLM
Display generated tokens incrementally in the chat interface
Add loading indicators for a better user experience
Handle interrupted or failed streaming requests gracefully
Verify smooth end-to-end streaming between backend and frontend
mechanism: Server-Sent Events (SSE) and HTTP chunked transfer encoding streaming tokens from LLM to frontend UI
purpose: Reducing time-to-first-token latency perception for users
ahaMoment: Streaming token delivery transforms perceived 5-second wait times into immediate responsive conversation.

title: Response Formatting & Rich Outputs
objectives: Add citations to chatbot responses using retrieved knowledge
Create structured cards for claims and coverage summaries
Render Markdown content with tables, lists, and formatting
Validate structured outputs before displaying them
Improve chatbot readability and response trustworthiness
mechanism: Structured JSON payload rendering into dynamic UI widgets (tables, cards, badges, inline citations)
purpose: Enhancing response readability, transparency, and clinical confidence
commonFailureModes: Invalid markdown rendering breaking card layout
Mismatch between text content and card metrics
ahaMoment: Inline citations back-linked directly to source documents turn speculative LLM answers into verifiable facts.

title: Conversation Memory & Context Management
objectives: Persist conversation history across multiple user sessions
Build context-aware conversations using previous messages
Implement automatic conversation summarization for long chats
Manage token limits while preserving important context
Ensure the chatbot remembers user preferences throughout a conversation
mechanism: Sliding window message buffer with periodic LLM conversation summarization
purpose: Maintaining long-term dialogue continuity without exceeding model context limits or exploding API costs
commonFailureModes: Context window overflow error on long chats
Key user details lost in aggressive compression
ahaMoment: Summarizing early dialogue history while keeping the last N turns verbatim gives infinite conversation depth within fixed token budgets.

title: Agentic Frameworks: LangChain Agents & Tool Use
objectives: Convert function-calling workflows into a reasoning agent
Wrap chatbot capabilities as reusable LangChain tools
Build a ReAct agent capable of selecting the correct tool automatically
Analyze reasoning traces to understand agent decision making
Evaluate whether the agent chooses the right tools for healthcare queries
mechanism: ReAct (Reason + Act) cognitive loop dynamically planning, selecting tools, executing, and observing results
purpose: Transitioning from rigid linear code pipelines to autonomous goal-directed decision making
commonFailureModes: Hallucinated tool selection when tools have ambiguous descriptions
ahaMoment: Writing precise tool docstrings is prompt engineering for agent tool selection—clear tool descriptions double agent accuracy.

title: Multi-Agent Orchestration
objectives: Create specialized agents for different healthcare domains
Build a router agent that delegates requests to the correct specialist
Implement a complete multi-agent workflow
Compare multi-agent performance with a single-agent architecture
Identify scenarios where multiple agents provide measurable benefits
mechanism: Directed Acyclic Graph (DAG) state graph orchestrating communication between specialized agent personas
purpose: Solving complex multi-domain healthcare queries through specialized expert collaboration
commonFailureModes: High latency accumulation from sequential agent calls
ahaMoment: Specializing agents with restricted tools and distinct system prompts performs better than one bloated super-agent trying to do everything.

title: Model Context Protocol (MCP)
objectives: Understand the purpose of the Model Context Protocol
Build an MCP server exposing healthcare chatbot tools
Connect the MCP server to an MCP-compatible client
Expose multiple chatbot capabilities through standardized MCP tools
Verify successful tool execution through live MCP interactions
mechanism: Open standard protocol (JSON-RPC over stdio/SSE) connecting AI models to client-side tools and data sources
purpose: Universal standardized integration layer between AI assistants and local/remote healthcare tools without custom wrapper code
ahaMoment: MCP decouples tool creation from client applications—build an MCP healthcare server once, connect to Claude, VS Code, or web frontends instantly.

title: Agentic Chatbot Integration
objectives: Integrate agents, MCP tools, retrieval, and conversation memory
Replace mock tools with live MCP-powered tool calls
Implement retries, timeouts, and graceful error handling
Perform failure testing to validate chatbot reliability
Build a production-style agentic chatbot pipeline
mechanism: Production-grade enterprise agent pipeline combining MCP protocol, stateful memory, and resilient error recovery handlers
purpose: Hardening agentic AI systems for real-world production reliability
commonFailureModes: Cascade failures when downstream MCP tool times out
ahaMoment: Building robust fallback handlers for failed tool calls makes agentic systems resilient enough for mission-critical enterprise use.

title: Chatbot Evaluation & Testing
objectives: Create a benchmark dataset covering representative healthcare questions
Evaluate chatbot responses for accuracy, grounding, and consistency
Measure retrieval quality and end-to-end response performance
Identify common failure cases and document improvement areas
Establish baseline metrics before production deployment
mechanism: LLM-as-a-judge automated benchmarking testing factual accuracy, grounding recall, and hallucinations
purpose: Continuous quality control and objective regression testing for AI pipelines
commonFailureModes: Benchmark dataset leakage into training/prompt exemplars
ahaMoment: Systematic automated benchmark evaluation is the only way to safely make prompt or model changes without introducing silent regressions.

title: Performance Optimization & Cost Management
objectives: Measure token usage across the chatbot pipeline
Optimize retrieval and prompt size to reduce latency and cost
Implement response caching for repeated queries
Benchmark response time before and after optimization
Document performance improvements using measurable metrics
mechanism: Prompt token trimming, semantic caching, and token budget management
purpose: Reducing API expenditure and latency while keeping answer quality high
commonFailureModes: Semantic cache false positive matches returning wrong answers
ahaMoment: Caching common queries reduces LLM API costs by up to 40% with 0ms latency.

title: Security, Privacy & Guardrails
objectives: Secure chatbot APIs against unauthorized access
Validate and sanitize user inputs before processing
Protect sensitive healthcare information throughout the pipeline
Implement prompt-injection and jailbreak safeguards
Test common security scenarios and document mitigation strategies
mechanism: Input sanitization filters, PII/PHI anonymization regex, and prompt injection classifier guardrails
purpose: Preventing data breaches, HIPAA violations, prompt injection exploits, and model jailbreaks
commonFailureModes: System prompt leakage via indirect prompt injection
Bypassing input validation via unicode encoding tricks
ahaMoment: Security must be enforced in code wrappers outside the LLM—never rely solely on system prompt instructions for security boundaries!

title: Docker & Kubernetes Deployment
objectives: Containerize the chatbot backend and frontend using Docker
Deploy the application to a Kubernetes cluster
Configure health checks and environment variables
Verify the deployed chatbot functions correctly
Prepare the application for production hosting
mechanism: Multi-stage Docker container build and Kubernetes pod orchestration with ingress routing
purpose: Cloud-native containerized deployment with auto-scaling and zero-downtime rolling updates
commonFailureModes: Missing environment variables in k8s secrets
Liveness probe failure killing starting container
ahaMoment: Multi-stage Docker builds reduce container sizes from 2GB to 150MB, speeding up deployment rollouts tenfold.

title: Monitoring, Logging & Observability
objectives: Add structured logging throughout the chatbot pipeline
Monitor API performance and chatbot usage
Track failures, latency, and tool execution metrics
Build dashboards for production observability
Use monitoring insights to improve chatbot reliability
mechanism: OpenTelemetry structured logging and Prometheus metrics collection exposed on /metrics endpoint
purpose: Real-time operational visibility into production AI system performance, cost, and error rates
commonFailureModes: High cardinality metrics exploding TSDB storage
Missing log correlation IDs across async requests
ahaMoment: Tracking latency histograms per pipeline step instantly reveals whether slowness comes from vector search, database queries, or LLM generation.

title: Production Readiness & Final Testing
objectives: Perform complete end-to-end testing of the chatbot
Validate retrieval, agent workflows, and frontend integration
Fix production issues discovered during testing
Complete deployment and operational documentation
Prepare the chatbot for real-world production usage
mechanism: End-to-end smoke testing, chaos testing, and production config verification
purpose: Final hardening and operational sign-off before capstone demonstration
commonFailureModes: Environment variable mismatch between staging and prod
ahaMoment: Rigorous end-to-end testing under simulated production failure conditions ensures total peace of mind during live demos.

title: Capstone Project & Final Demo
objectives: Demonstrate the complete enterprise healthcare chatbot
Showcase retrieval, RAG, agents, MCP, and conversation memory
Present the deployed application with production architecture
Evaluate the chatbot using real-world scenarios
Publish the final project with source code and documentation
mechanism: Integrated capstone demonstration of full 31-day AI engineering stack
purpose: Showcasing end-to-end mastery of building, securing, and deploying enterprise-grade AI systems
commonFailureModes: Live demo failure due to unhandled API rate limit
ahaMoment: Integrating all 31 days of knowledge into one cohesive healthcare chatbot proves complete mastery from data ingestion to production Kubernetes deployment.
